description: Standalone `foreach` binding behavior, templates, and else-chain state.

behaviors.statement: `foreach` accepts a plain array, `observableArray`, plain observable holding an array, or computed returning an array.
Initial render is synchronous even when `ForEachBinding.setSync(false)` is configured; later updates can be asynchronous.
`foreach` binds immediate children, nested descendants, and virtual-element templates.
`foreach: { name: "id", data: ... }` resolves templates by `id` from `<template>`, `<script type="text/ko-template">`, and regular DOM elements.
Empty lists set `elseChainSatisfied()` false; non-empty lists set it true, and that flag updates as the array is filled or emptied.
Array mutation, reordering, duplicate values, `$index`, `as`, and `noIndex` are all exercised in spec coverage.

`foreach` supports `afterRender(nodes, value)`, `beforeMove(node, newIndex, value)`, and `afterMove(node, newIndex, value)` lifecycle callbacks in addition to the existing batch-shaped `afterAdd` and `beforeRemove` callbacks.

Array changes made synchronously from `foreach` callbacks while a change batch is rendered (e.g. `afterRender` pushing or removing items, including during the initial render) are processed in a follow-up pass instead of being dropped.

With `as`, `foreach` extends the current context by default; when `options.createChildContextWithAs` is enabled it creates a child context per item (`$data` is the item, `$parent` the outer data, observable items unwrapped with the observable as `$rawData`).
